subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what token containment, read-target, and scope rules should it use?
rationale: The feature is valid but security-sensitive because it handles event-scoped Slack action tokens and workspace search results, and prior adjacent PRs used a different user-token search API with unresolved authorization concerns.

options.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, redaction, read-target policy, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack search
options.body: Define one Slack search contract covering RTS and user-token search, then land a focused implementation against that maintainer-approved contract.

options.title: Defer workspace search
options.body: Keep Slack workspace search out until maintainers are ready to own the token, privacy, scope, and live-validation burden.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, redaction, read-target policy, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Slack assistant/action history and the linked action-parity closure both route this product/security decision through this contributor's area history.
